chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man enters into a manumission contract (kitabah) with his slave, frees him, and he knows that the slave has wealth, and the master did not reserve the wealth when he freed him, then the wealth belongs to the slave.

key_terms.كاتب: A slave who has a contract to buy his own freedom

ai.seo_question: Does the master keep the slave's wealth if he frees him without reserving it?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the default legal presumption in manumission contracts (kitabah): unless the master explicitly reserves the slave's existing wealth, it automatically transfers to the slave upon freedom. This ruling underscores the principle of preserving the slave's financial autonomy and prevents masters from arbitrarily claiming property that the slave had accumulated, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise contractual stipulations in civil transactions.
